projectsObjects.title: Δυµαχω
projectsObjects.subtitle: From Paper to Platform
projectsObjects.description:
This project was carried out during the second semester of the first year of our studies at the Utrecht University of Applied Sciences, in collaboration with a team of five students. The problem statement was provided by the company Dumaco Oss. Although we were not yet allowed to actively collaborate with external companies at that stage, their case served as the foundation for our project. As a result, we chose our own project name, inspired by the name Dumaco in Ancient Greek.

The goal of the project was to optimize internal processes at Dumaco, with a specific focus on the order slip process. At the time, this process was still entirely paper-based, which often led to inefficiencies and errors. Our solution involved digitizing the process by developing a custom web application with an integrated database. Additionally, there was limited visibility into the location of products and their corresponding pallets within the factory. We conducted research into potential solutions for this issue as well and developed a proof of concept.

Throughout the project, we worked with many new technologies. As a result, we built a solution that lacked a solid foundation, but this also provided valuable learning experiences. We reflected on this and identified concrete areas for improvement to apply in future projects. For the technical implementation, we used React for the frontend, and Node.js with JavaScript and a MySQL database for the backend.

projectsObjects.title: Party Plaza
projectsObjects.subtitle: A minecraft project
projectsObjects.description:
Party Plaza is a hobby project I started with a friend, focused on creating a Minecraft server featuring multiple minigames in a tournament format. The goal is to provide a flexible environment where players can sign up for tournaments and experience a variety of games, from PvP battles to puzzle challenges.

The project is built in Java using Maven, with a main plugin managing all minigames. A key technical feature is the two-way communication between the main plugin and the minigames, allowing the main plugin to start games and manage teams, while minigames can send information back. This modular approach ensures that minigames can operate independently but are still centrally controlled.

Currently, the first test runs have been completed with two minigames. The final plan is to implement six games with a rotation system to keep each tournament unique. While I develop most of the project myself, my friend contributed to setting up the initial framework and acquiring essential knowledge.

Future plans include expanding Party Plaza with new minigames and features, leveraging the modular design for easy maintenance and adaptation. This project demonstrates my skills in Java development, plugin architecture, and creating scalable, modular systems.

projectsObjects.title: Portfolio Website
projectsObjects.subtitle: Showcasing my work and skills
projectsObjects.description:
This portfolio website is a personal project I built entirely on my own to provide a comprehensive overview of my professional profile. The website is designed to showcase my CV, completed projects, and educational background, while offering visitors a clear and structured way to explore my work and skills.

Technically, the site is built using React with TypeScript, ensuring a modern, component-based architecture. One of the key design choices was to structure all content through JSON files, enabling easy updates, additions, and translations without modifying the core codebase. Each language version is fully supported via separate JSON configurations, allowing seamless multilingual functionality and dynamic content rendering.

The website emphasizes modularity, maintainability, and scalability. Projects and other sections are dynamically loaded from the JSON data, reducing duplication and improving consistency across the site. This approach not only streamlines content management but also demonstrates best practices in structuring a React application for flexibility and future expansion.

Building this project allowed me to strengthen my skills in React, TypeScript, and JSON-driven dynamic architectures, while creating a practical platform to present my portfolio in a professional and user-friendly way. The site is fully adaptable, maintainable, and ready to grow as my skills and projects evolve.

projectsObjects.title: Cuimed
projectsObjects.subtitle: From Research to a Secure Ordering Platform
projectsObjects.description:
This project was carried out during the first semester of our second year of study as a group internship project. Our team consisted of six students, and the project was the main focus of our time throughout the semester. The project was carried out for Cuimed, a company that imports primarily Spanish products and sells them to high-end restaurants. Because we were working with a real company, the project gave us the opportunity to work on a solution that could have a genuine impact on their business.

The main objective was to investigate and optimize several of Cuimed's business processes. We started by focusing on the ordering process and explored how this could be improved through a dedicated customer portal. One of the important requirements was that Cuimed's customers should be able to view and order products without competitors being able to access the product range or pricing information. Based on our research, we decided to develop a proof of concept for a secure web-based ordering platform.

The resulting application was designed as a webshop where Cuimed's customers could browse products and place orders. Although the complete application was not finished within the project period, we successfully developed a working proof of concept that demonstrated how the proposed solution could work. A significant part of the project consisted of researching Cuimed's existing processes and translating our findings into a feasible technical solution.

For the technical implementation, we used React for the frontend, Python for the backend, and PostgreSQL as the database. We also used Docker to set up an OTAP environment and integrated this workflow with GitHub. I was primarily responsible for the backend development and was also the Scrum Master of the team. This gave me the opportunity to further develop both my technical skills and my understanding of Agile project management.

One of the most valuable aspects of this project was working for a real company and seeing how our work could potentially have a real impact. Technically, I learned a great deal about Docker and setting up an OTAP environment through GitHub. As Scrum Master, I also gained experience in facilitating the team's development process and taking responsibility for keeping the team organized. Like any student project, we encountered mistakes and challenges along the way, but working through these problems was an important part of the learning experience.

projectsObjects.title: Bingo
projectsObjects.subtitle: From Challenges to Code
projectsObjects.description:
Bingo is a personal project that I started at the beginning of 2026 outside of my studies. The idea originated from a tradition within my friend group, where we create a yearly bingo card containing various challenges that we want to complete throughout the year. Keeping track of these challenges manually became inconvenient, which led me to develop my own application to make the process easier and more interactive.

The application allows users to create their own bingo cards and add custom challenges to them. These cards can then be used within groups, where members can mark their completed challenges and keep track of their progress. Users can also view the bingo cards of other members in their group, making it possible to see how everyone is progressing. The application supports multiple groups, allowing users to participate in different bingo groups at the same time.

I developed the entire application independently, from the frontend to the backend and database. The frontend was built using React and TypeScript, while the backend uses NestJS and TypeORM with a PostgreSQL database. Docker is used for deployment and to manage the different components of the application. NestJS and TypeORM were both new frameworks for me, making the project a valuable opportunity to expand my technical knowledge and experiment with technologies I had not previously used.

One of the most valuable aspects of this project has been learning how to take an application beyond development and actually make it available to users. This included learning more about deployment, managing a live application, and considering how users interact with the system. Since I developed the entire application myself, I was responsible for all technical decisions and implementations.

The application is currently in an early but functional stage and is already usable by my own group. Development is still ongoing, with the goal of eventually making the application suitable for anyone who wants to create and participate in their own challenge-based bingo games. This makes Bingo both a practical project for my own needs and an ongoing opportunity to further develop my skills as a developer.

projectsObjects.title: Belastingdienst
projectsObjects.subtitle: Exploring AI for Smarter Tax Processing
projectsObjects.description:
This project was carried out during the second semester of my second year of study in collaboration with the Dutch Tax and Customs Administration (Belastingdienst). The project was part of a team of six students, and I took on the role of Product Owner. During the project, I also worked as a temporary government employee, which gave me the opportunity to experience working within a large public organization. The assignment was carried out within department IV for CAP, with the ultimate goal of supporting the LH department.

Within LH, approximately 50,000 requests are submitted each year for Melding Loonheffingen Aanmelding werkgever. Processing these requests can be a time-consuming task for employees. The goal of our project was to investigate whether artificial intelligence could be used to support employees by automatically providing suggestions during this process. By reducing the amount of manual work, employees could potentially process requests more efficiently and spend more time on other tasks.

Our main focus was to determine whether an AI-based solution could provide useful and reliable suggestions. We researched and experimented with several open-source AI models and fine-tuned them using Python. One of the approaches we investigated used vector spaces to classify descriptions into the appropriate sectors. Instead of providing a single result, the system generated a top three or top five selection of possible sectors. In our tests, the correct sector was included in the generated suggestions approximately 90% of the time.

The final result was a successful proof of concept demonstrating that AI could potentially be used to support this process. Although the solution was not intended to replace employees or fully automate the process, it showed that AI could provide useful suggestions that could make the work of LH employees more efficient.

My role in this project was primarily focused on managing the team and the overall project as Product Owner. I was responsible for planning the work, monitoring progress, identifying obstacles within the team, and helping to resolve them. I was also responsible for quality control of the products created by the team and conducted several research activities myself. Rather than contributing directly to the development of the AI models, my focus was on ensuring that the team's work remained aligned with the project's goals and requirements.

One of the most valuable aspects of this project was experiencing what it is like to work within a large organization where responsibilities are highly specialized and employees have extensive expertise in their respective fields. Working with the Belastingdienst gave me a better understanding of how professional organizations approach complex problems and collaborate across different areas of expertise. More than anything, I am proud of the personal growth I experienced during this project, particularly in my ability to take responsibility for a project and lead a team within a large professional organization.

projectsObjects.title: Scouting Warehouse
projectsObjects.subtitle: From WhatsApp to Warehouse Management
projectsObjects.description:
Scouting Warehouse is a personal project that I started in May of 2026 for Scouting Drunen, also known as the Dr. Akkermans group. The project originated from a practical problem within the organization: equipment in the scouting warehouse was being reserved through a WhatsApp group. While this was a simple solution, it often resulted in reservations being forgotten or not communicated properly, which could cause multiple groups to reserve the same equipment. There was also no clear way to report damaged or broken equipment, meaning that problems could remain unnoticed.

The goal of Scouting Warehouse is to create a central application for managing the equipment within the scouting organization. Users will be able to view available equipment, reserve items for specific dates, and borrow equipment from the warehouse. The application will also provide a way to report problems with equipment, allowing damaged items to be identified and eventually repaired or removed from circulation. By centralizing these processes, the application should reduce conflicts between different scouting sections and make managing the warehouse easier.

The project is being developed as a free solution for the organization, with the intention of keeping it accessible to scouting groups with limited budgets. Rather than creating a commercial product, the focus is on solving a real problem in a practical and accessible way. The project is still under active development, with the basic foundation already in place, but significant work remains before it can be fully used within the organization.

For the technical implementation, I am using Next.js and React. I am developing the entire application myself, while a professional DevOps developer helps with the deployment and reviews my work. This provides me with an opportunity to learn not only how to build an application, but also how professional developers approach code quality, deployment, and software development practices.

One of the main reasons I started this project was to become more involved with my scouting organization while combining this with my interest in software development. By solving a real problem within the organization, I can directly see how technology can make existing processes easier. At the same time, the project challenges me to create something that people will actually want to use, rather than simply building a technically functional application.

The project is still in development and will require several major steps before it is ready for real-world use. However, the basic foundation has been established, and the continued development of Scouting Warehouse gives me the opportunity to further improve my coding practices and learn how software development is approached in a professional environment.
